documented: Primary (Microsoft 8-K EX-99.1, public 16:03 ET): Q2 revenue $62.02bn, diluted EPS $2.93, Azure +30% (+28% in constant currency), above the 26-27% cc guidance Microsoft gave on 24 Oct 2023.

Primary (Microsoft call transcript, 30 Jan 2024, after the release): Q3 guidance of Intelligent Cloud $26.0-26.3bn, Productivity $19.3-19.6bn, More Personal Computing $14.7-15.1bn; Azure growth in cc 'to remain stable' with Q2.
Primary (Federal Reserve, 31 Jan 2024, 14:00 ET): FOMC held the target range at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2% and said it did not expect to cut 'until it has gained greater confidence' on inflation.

Press (CNBC, Wed 31 Jan 2024 16:24 ET, written after the close): 'Microsoft and AMD slipped nearly 3% each on lower-than-expected forward guidance'. That is CNBC's attribution. The article does not quote a pre-event consensus for the guidance.
Press (CNBC, 31 Jan 2024): S&P 500 -1.61%, Nasdaq Composite -2.23%. This system measures -1.611% and -2.230%, an exact match.
inference: Most of MSFT's -2.69% on 31 Jan is consistent with market and tech-sector movement. With beta 1.20 the market-model abnormal return is only -0.86% (-0.7 sigma), inside normal daily noise. XLK (-2.10%) and QQQ (-1.96%) also fell; MSFT is itself a large XLK constituent (index weight not tracked here), which damps the sector-adjusted figure.

The overnight gap (-0.40%; QQQ -1.05% over the same window) came before the 14:00 FOMC statement. The -2.30% regular session spans it. Without intraday data the post-FOMC share of the decline cannot be measured.

The press narrative ('lower-than-expected guidance') cannot be tested here: no point-in-time consensus for FY24 Q3 segment revenue was found, so 'light' is a characterisation, not a measured surprise.

Earlier statements in this conversation implied a significant negative reaction to the earnings. The corrected reading is that the reaction was not statistically distinguishable from market and sector moves that day.

documented: Primary (Alphabet 8-K, 16:01 ET): Q4 2023 revenue $86.31bn, diluted EPS $1.64; Alphabet does not issue quantitative guidance (no outlook section in its prior-quarter release).

Press (CNBC, page updated 30 Jan 17:49 ET): ad revenue '$65.52 billion trailed analysts' estimates of $65.94 billion, according to StreetAccount'. This is a grade-C expectation (documented after the event).
inference: Unlike MSFT, the GOOGL move is large relative to its own noise: -5.30% abnormal (-3.5 sigma), and -5.18% happened in the overnight gap, before the FOMC statement. That timing favours a company-specific explanation for most of the decline.

The ad-revenue shortfall against StreetAccount is a plausible driver, but StreetAccount's estimate is only documented after the event (grade C) and the dated pre-event Zacks consensus is on a different (ex-TAC) basis, so the surprise cannot be measured cleanly.

documented: Primary (Meta 8-K, 16:10 ET, Items 2.02/8.01/9.01): Q4 2023 revenue $40.1bn, above the $36.5-40bn range Meta guided on 25 Oct 2023; first quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share announced in the same release.
Press (CNBC, 2 Feb 2024): 'Meta shares closed up more than 20% on Friday'. Measured: +20.32%.
inference: The +18.1% abnormal return (9 sigma) is far outside normal noise. The 08:30 ET payrolls release fell inside the overnight-gap window, but SPY rose only +1.05% on the day, so macro news cannot account for the move's magnitude.
Revenue above the top of guidance and the first dividend arrived together in one document. This data cannot separate their effects.

documented: Primary (Meta 8-K, 16:19 ET): Q3 2022 revenue $27.71bn, inside the $26-28.5bn range guided on 27 Jul 2022; 2023 total expenses outlook $96-101bn.
Press (CNBC, 27 Oct 2022): 'Shares of Meta plunged 24.5% Thursday'. Measured: -24.56%.
inference: Revenue was within guidance and roughly at the dated Zacks consensus, while diluted EPS was ~10% below the Zacks consensus. The size of the reaction (-23.4% abnormal, -9.3 sigma, almost all in the overnight gap) suggests the market reacted to forward cost commitments rather than to the quarter's revenue. That is a hypothesis: no point-in-time consensus for 2023 expenses is in the registry.

documented: Primary (Alphabet 8-K, 16:01 ET): Q3 2023 revenue $76.69bn, diluted EPS $1.55.
Press (CNBC, page updated 25 Oct 2023): Google Cloud revenue '$8.41 billion vs. $8.64 billion, according to StreetAccount' (grade C). The dated pre-event Zacks Cloud consensus was $8.54bn (grade B).
Measured, same evening: MSFT also reported after the close on 24 Oct 2023 and rose +3.07% on 25 Oct, while GOOGL fell -9.51%.
inference: Opposite moves by two mega-caps that reported in the same post-close window argue against a common market factor. The -7.5% abnormal return (-4.8 sigma) is most plausibly company-specific; the Cloud shortfall against both the dated Zacks estimate and StreetAccount is the documented candidate.

documented: Primary (Microsoft 8-K, 16:04 ET): Azure +33% (+34% in constant currency), above the 28-29% cc guidance given on 30 Jul 2024.
Primary (Microsoft call transcript, 30 Oct 2024): 'In Azure, we expect Q2 revenue growth to be 31% to 32% in constant currency'.
Press (CNBC, 31 Oct 2024): 'Microsoft shares fell more than 6% on Thursday after guidance fell short of analysts' estimates'. Measured: -6.05%.
inference: The decline is mostly idiosyncratic (-3.9% abnormal, -4.4 sigma) and followed results that beat both the dated Zacks consensus and Microsoft's own Azure guidance. That pattern is consistent with the press attribution to forward guidance, but the pre-event consensus for Q2 Azure growth is not documented point-in-time, so it remains a hypothesis.
META reported in the same window and fell -4.09% the same day. The PCE release on the morning of 31 Oct 2024 (tracked by this system from ALFRED vintage dates) also falls inside the overnight window.
